summary: Risk-on follow-through on jobs day. The July payrolls report cleared at 8:30 AM ET and stocks rallied. NQ reclaimed its trend and closed 29,841 (+1.14%); ES flipped its trend back long and closed 7,777.25 (+0.59%), so the laggard caught up. All four opening ranges broke down first at the US open, a quick shakeout, then the indices reversed and ran higher into the close. Gold was the standout, ripping +2.37% to 4,368.5 and flipping its trend long, with spot gold +2.39% and silver +3.19%. Crude gave back -1.48% to 77.09 after Thursday's spike but held just above its stop. The VIX eased to 14.90 and the 10-year yield slipped to about 4.66%.
psychology: Today rewarded traders who did not panic on the open. All four markets broke the bottom of their opening range in the first few minutes, the exact moment a lot of people hit sell or bail on longs, and then price turned and ran the other way. That is a bear trap, and it happens most on event days like a jobs report, when the first move is often noise before the real move sets in. The lesson is not always fade the open. The lesson is that the first five minutes after a big number is the lowest-quality information of the day, and your plan should already know that. If your rule is to wait for two hourly closes beyond a level, the opening shakeout is not even a decision, it is just noise you were built to ignore.

event.name: July jobs report clears, market rallies, metals rip
event.consensus: The July jobs report (nonfarm payrolls) was the highest-impact release of the week, due Friday at 8:30 AM ET.
event.actual: The number cleared and stocks rallied. NQ reclaimed its trend to close +1.14% and ES flipped back long to close +0.59%, so the two indices moved up together. The 10-year yield slipped to about 4.66% and the VIX eased to 14.90.
event.surprise: The market took the jobs data as risk-on. The opening ranges broke down first then reversed up, a classic event-day bear-trap.
event.nqReaction: NQ fell into the open, broke the bottom of its opening range at 14:00 UTC to 29,619, then reversed and climbed all session to close 29,841, above both its stop and its average.
event.crossAsset: Gold ripped +2.37% to 4,368.5 and flipped its trend long, with spot gold +2.39% and silver a strong +3.19%, a broad precious-metals bid. Crude gave back -1.48% to 77.09 after Thursday's +4.26% spike but held just above its stop.

risk.sizing: Volatility eased again, with the VIX near 14.90 and NQ's ATR down to 106.16, so risk per contract is a touch smaller. The board is aligned to the upside, which is easier to trade than yesterday's split, but do not confuse alignment with a free pass. ES and gold flipped long only today, so those are day-one signals: size them down and let a pullback come to you rather than chasing the highs.
risk.openRisk: Three markets are confirmed longs: NQ above 29,609, ES above 7,745, and gold above 4,332. Crude is the odd one out, still long by only 0.33 above 76.76 after closing red, so treat it as the most likely to flip and stand aside on longs until it reclaims its 77.86 average.
risk.note: The week's main event is July CPI on Wednesday, August 12 at 8:30 AM ET, which can reprice every one of these levels in seconds. Monday is quiet, so use it to plan exposure into CPI, not to over-trade. Watch whether NQ holds its 29,761 average, whether ES builds on its fresh long above 7,745, and whether crude loses or reclaims its 76.76 stop. Check your prop-firm blackout rules around CPI.
